items.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023
items.q: and even the Jimi Hendrix Experience would be playing in local bars, you know, in the back room or upstairs. There were no dressing rooms let alone bouncers. And you’d see someone at the bar and you’d take your tenor along

ctx.x: I was curious, there’s anecdotes that you’ve shared about, probably not that long after that, sitting in with some of the now-well-known rock bands. You’d go to a club and, did you have to like make your way through the bouncers and the manager or whatever?

No the interesting thing is there weren’t any in those days, and we’re talking about, you know, bands like Fleetwood Mac and John Mayall’s Bluesbreakers and even the Jimi Hendrix Experience would be playing in local bars, you know, in the back room or upstairs. There were no dressing rooms let alone bouncers. And you’d see someone at the bar and you’d take your tenor along, or I’d take my tenor along, and I’d say, “Can I play with you?” And quite usually they would say yeah, sure. And it wasn’t a case of well we…
Nice deal. When you got up on the stage, would they usually call one of their originals or would they do like a blues or something?
